content.value_statement: Marketing choices often rely on guesses about why people buy. This skill applies behavioral science and mental models to improve messaging, pricing, onboarding, and conversion decisions.
actual_capabilities: Maps marketing problems to relevant mental models such as anchoring, social proof, scarcity, and loss aversion.
Explains the psychology behind each model in plain language.
Suggests ethical marketing applications for pricing pages, onboarding flows, copy, and campaigns.
Uses product marketing context files when available to tailor recommendations.
Provides task-specific questions that clarify audience, journey stage, and behavior goals.
Cross-references related skills for CRO, copywriting, popups, pricing, and A/B testing.
limitations: It gives strategic guidance, not validated customer research or legal advice.
It cannot prove that a psychology tactic will improve results without testing.
It does not build experiments, analytics, designs, or production campaign assets by itself.
It should not be used to create false scarcity, deceptive urgency, or misleading claims.

use_cases.title: Improve Pricing Framing
use_cases.description: Use anchoring, price relativity, and social proof to improve a B2B SaaS pricing page.

use_cases.title: Increase Activation
use_cases.description: Apply Goal-Gradient, Hick's Law, and commitment models to reduce friction in onboarding.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Campaign Problems
use_cases.description: Use inversion, constraints, and first principles to identify why a campaign is underperforming.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Relevant Models
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner model selection for a clear marketing challenge.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am working on [marketing challenge] for [audience]. Identify the best mental models to apply. Explain each model and give practical next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Pricing Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate guidance for pricing and plan comparison.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pricing structure: [plans and prices]. Apply pricing psychology ethically. Recommend changes using anchoring, framing, social proof, and loss aversion.

prompt_templates.title: Design Ethical Persuasion
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for messaging or campaign strategy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me influence [target behavior] without deception. Choose relevant psychology principles. Include ethical boundaries, customer risks, and examples of acceptable messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Funnel
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis across funnel stages and user motivations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this funnel: [journey details]. Identify the main behavioral bottlenecks. Use at least five mental models and prioritize the highest impact fixes.

output_examples.input: How can I reduce decision paralysis on our pricing page?
output: Apply Paradox of Choice by limiting tiers and highlighting one recommended plan.
Use Hick's Law to remove secondary calls to action near the purchase decision.
Support the recommendation with social proof near the plan comparison.

output_examples.input: Why do free trials convert better for some SaaS products?
output: Free trials create ownership through the endowment effect.
They also use loss aversion because users dislike losing access after activation.
Freemium works better when network effects or long adoption cycles matter more.

output_examples.input: Help me use scarcity in a launch email.
output: Use scarcity only when the limit is real, such as cohort capacity or a fixed bonus period.
State the reason for the limit clearly.
Avoid fake countdowns, invented waitlists, or pressure that hides important product details.

best_practices: Start with the behavior you want to influence before choosing a mental model.
Use real customer evidence to decide which psychological principle applies.
State ethical boundaries when using urgency, scarcity, defaults, or social proof.
anti_patterns: Using fake countdowns, false waitlists, or artificial limits to create pressure.
Applying many biases at once without a clear customer problem.
Treating psychology models as proof instead of hypotheses to test.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply behavioral science and mental models to marketing decisions, messaging, pricing, onboarding, and conversion problems.

faq.question: Does it create manipulative marketing?
faq.answer: No. It recommends ethical applications and warns against false scarcity, deceptive urgency, and misleading claims.

faq.question: Can it improve pricing pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest framing, anchoring, tier structure, social proof, and loss aversion ideas for pricing pages.

faq.question: Does it replace customer research?
faq.answer: No. It provides hypotheses and strategy guidance, but teams should validate ideas with customers and performance data.

faq.question: Can it design A/B tests?
faq.answer: It can form psychology-based hypotheses. A dedicated A/B testing skill is better for experiment design and analysis.
